precepts.text: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: that is the cooking fire, not the heat in winter. And stop following the additions of the Talmud from people who are not the real Jews.
precepts.point: On the seventh day God ended his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day. The seventh day is not Sunday. Seven represents completion, perfection; hold that, because the whole class hangs on it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Another law of the Sabbath: “Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.”

That is not talking about turning on the heat when it is freezing in the house. It is talking about cooking: do not kindle a fire to cook on the Sabbath. It goes together with Exodus 16:23, where the food is baked and boiled the day before and laid up until the morning.

And stop following Amalek, the so-called Jewish people who are not the real Jews, who add to the law with their Talmud, their oral law. Their additions make the Sabbath a burden God never put on it. The commandment is what is written: no cooking fire in our habitations on the day God blessed and sanctified, the seventh day on which he “rested from all his work which God created and made.”

precepts.text: Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; this speaks to the cooking fire, not to warming the household.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” This speaks to the cooking fire, not to warming the household.

Eating is allowed on the sabbath, but not cooking. No microwaving, no coffee pots, no kindling the cooking fire; the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food prepared the day before. It is the seventh day, “the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord”.

precepts.text: Bake that which ye will bake today, and lay up what remaineth to be kept until the morning; kindling fire on the sabbath goes to cooking, so the cooking was done on the preparation day.
precepts.point: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” Kindling fire goes to cooking. “To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

You could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day. What you bake and seethe that day is laid up, and what you prepare that day is what you eat on the seventh day, the holy day, the sabbath of rest to the Lord.

precepts.text: Kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day; that is fire for cooking, not the altar fire.
precepts.point: Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” That speaks of making food in your habitations, not the altar fire.

The burnt offering burned upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar was burning in it. The Levites were commanded to keep a fire burning on the altar continually, sabbath included, so the two commandments do not cross.

precepts.text: On the holy sabbath day whosoever doeth work shall be put to death, and ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations; no cooking on the Sabbath.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein.” Moses gave the same word to all the congregation: “Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord: whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.”

Then more than no working: “Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” So there is no cooking on the Sabbath. Keeping it holy is more than staying off the job.

And it is “the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.” No matter where your dwelling is, Israel, North America, London or Australia, the Sabbath is still the Sabbath: Friday sundown to Saturday sundown in whatever time zone you are in.

precepts.text: At the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness, both men and women as many as were willing hearted brought their gold unto the Lord; we have to have that same willing heart today.
precepts.point: Deborah and Barak sing praise to the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves. That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
Deborah and Barak praise the Lord “when the people willingly offered themselves.” The same willing heart was seen at the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness: “they came, both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, and brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold: and every man that offered offered an offering of gold unto the Lord.”

That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him. Men and women who were willing hearted brought their gold; the people in Deborah's day willingly offered themselves for the war. We have to have that same willing heart today.

precepts.text: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day, one of the precepts you must go through to see what work was actually forbidden.
precepts.point: They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” This is one of the precepts you have to go through to see what work was actually forbidden on the Sabbath.

Kindling a fire is the kind of work the law names. Healing a man is not, which is why the charge that Christ broke the Sabbath is the Pharisees' spirit, not the law.

points: Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: Every wise hearted among you shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded: those who had skill, the crafty ones.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: Both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, red skins of rams, badgers' skins, silver, brass, or shittim wood brought it.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: All the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands; the women knew how to sew, and brought that which they had spun of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats' hair. The rulers brought onyx stones, stones for the ephod and breastplate, spice, and oil.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; the Most High put His spirit on him to be gifted in what he did, to devise curious works in gold, silver, and brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of wood.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: He hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; the two brothers the Most High was dealing with in workmanship trained and taught their fellow brethren how to do it.

It is the same today: the Most High puts His spirit on brothers and sisters with different talents, and they put their talents to use and teach others in the congregation; Israel was putting their talents together and building, showing each other how to do these works.
